- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.3) in recent days, increase downward bias or add early correction to prevent overshoot.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast slope after peak.  
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon; apply downward bias of 1–2% for first 5–7 days.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling after peak), model should adjust downward faster.  
- Forecast should not exceed 3–4% above recent 7-day high unless sentiment strongly bullish.  
- If sentiment history shows no clear trend (mostly 0.00), forecast should be conservative and not assume continuation of prior trend.
